shloka_text: एवं सञ्चिन्त्य विप्रेन्दो जगाम लघुविक्रमः । आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति ।। 7.21.1 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ sañcintya viprendo jagāma laghuvikramaḥ | ākhyātuṃ tadyathāvṛttaṃ yamasya sadanaṃ prati || 7.21.1 ||
translation: एवम् thus, सञ्चिन्त्य having thought, विप्रेन्दो the best of Brahmins (Narada), जगाम went, लघुविक्रमः with swift steps, आख्यातुम् to tell, तत् that, यथावृत्तम् as it happened, यमस्य of Yama, सदनम् abode, प्रति towards,
explanation: Having thus pondered, Narada, moving swiftly, went towards Yama's abode to narrate the events as they had transpired.
comments: Narada hastens ahead to forewarn Yama -- entering Yama's realm, Ravana beholds the torments of the damned and the bliss of the righteous and sets free those being punished -- Yama's hosts fall upon him, and in the great battle Ravana's son, wielding the Pashupata weapon, consumes Yama's army with fire.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम् । विधानमुपतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम् ।। 7.21.2 ।।
transliteration: apaśyatsa yamaṃ tatra devamagnipuraskṛtam | vidhānamupatiṣṭhantaṃ prāṇino yasya yādṛśam || 7.21.2 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, स he, यमम् Yama, तत्र there, देवम् the god, अग्निपुरस्कृतम् with fire placed in front, विधानम् the ordinance, उपतिष्ठन्तम् administering, प्राणिनो of beings, यस्य whose, यादृशम् as it is,
explanation: There, Narada saw the god Yama, honored by fire, administering the fate of all beings as it was ordained for each.

shloka_text: स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम् । अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः ।। 7.21.3 ।।
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṃ maharṣiṃ tatra nāradam | abravītsukhamāsīnamarghyamāvedya dharmataḥ || 7.21.3 ||
translation: स he, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, यमः Yama, प्राप्तम् arrived, महर्षिम् the great sage, तत्र there, नारदम् Narada, अब्रवीत् he spoke, सुखमासीनम् comfortably seated, अर्घ्यम् water offering, आवेद्य having offered, धर्मतः according to dharma,
explanation: Upon seeing the great sage Narada arrive there, Yama, having properly offered him a water offering and seated him comfortably, then spoke.

shloka_text: कच्चित्क्षेमं तु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति । किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित ।। 7.21.4 ।।
transliteration: kaccitkṣemaṃ tu devarṣe kacciddharmo na naśyati | kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ te devagandharvasevita || 7.21.4 ||
translation: कच्चित् is it that, क्षेमम् well-being, तु indeed, देवर्षे O divine sage, कच्चित् is it that, धर्मो dharma, न not, नश्यति perishes, किम् what, आगमनकृत्यम् purpose of arrival, ते your, देवगन्धर्वसेवित O one served by gods and gandharvas,
explanation: Yama asked, "O divine sage, is all well with you, and is dharma not perishing? What is the purpose of your visit, O one revered by gods and gandharvas?"

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः । श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम् ।। 7.21.5 ।।
transliteration: abravīttu tadā vākyaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ | śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi vidhānaṃ ca vidhīyatām || 7.21.5 ||
translation: अब्रवीत् spoke, तु indeed, तदा then, वाक्यं words, नारदः Narada, भगवान् revered, ऋषिः sage, श्रूयताम् listen, अभिधास्यामि I will tell, विधानं the plan, च and, विधीयताम् let it be done.
explanation: Then, the revered sage Narada spoke these words: "Listen, I will tell you the plan, and let it be carried out."

shloka_text: एष नाम्नो दशग्रीवः पितृराज निशाचरः । उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रमैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम् ।। 7.21.6 ।।
transliteration: eṣa nāmno daśagrīvaḥ pitṛrāja niśācaraḥ | upayāti vaśaṃ netuṃ vikramaistvāṃ sudurjayam || 7.21.6 ||
translation: एषः this one, नाम्नः by name, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, पितृराज O King of Pitrus, निशाचरः the demon, उपयाति approaches, वशं under control, नेतुं to bring, विक्रमैः by his valor, त्वां you, सुदुर्जयम् who are very difficult to conquer.
explanation: O King of Pitrus, this demon named Dashagriva is approaching to bring you, who are very difficult to conquer, under his control through his valor.

shloka_text: एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो । दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति ।। 7.21.7 ।।
transliteration: etena kāraṇenāhaṃ tvarito hyāgataḥ prabho | daṇḍapraharaṇasyādya tava kiṃ nu bhaviṣyati || 7.21.7 ||
translation: एतेन by this, कारणेन reason, अहं I, त्वरितः quickly, हि indeed, आगतः have come, प्रभो O Lord, दण्डप्रहरणस्य of the wielder of the staff, अद्य today, तव your, किं what, नु indeed, भविष्यति will happen.
explanation: O Lord, it is for this reason that I have quickly come; what will happen today to you, the wielder of the staff of punishment?

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दुरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम् । ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.21.8 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare durādaṃśumantamivoditam | dadṛśurdīptamāyāntaṃ vimānaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ || 7.21.8 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, अन्तरे interval, दुरात् from afar, अंशुमन्तम् the sun, इव like, उदितम् risen, ददृशुः they saw, दीप्तम् shining, आयान्तं coming, विमानं the aerial chariot, तस्य his, रक्षसः of the demon.
explanation: In the meantime, from afar, they saw the demon's radiant aerial chariot approaching, shining like the rising sun.

shloka_text: तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः । कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.21.9 ।।
transliteration: taṃ deśaṃ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ | kṛtvā vitimiraṃ sarvaṃ samīpaṃ so 'bhyavartata || 7.21.9 ||
translation: तं that, देशं region, प्रभया by the radiance, तस्य of that, पुष्पकस्य Pushpaka, महाबलः the mighty one, कृत्वा having made, वितिमिरं free from darkness, सर्वं all, समीपं near, सः he, अभ्यवर्तत approached.
explanation: The mighty one, Ravana, having illuminated the entire region with the radiance of his Pushpaka chariot, then approached that place.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः । प्राणिनः सुकृतं कर्म भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम् ।। 7.21.10 ।।
transliteration: so 'paśyatsa mahābāhurdaśagrīvastatastataḥ | prāṇinaḥ sukṛtaṃ karma bhuñjānāṃścaiva duṣkṛtam || 7.21.10 ||
translation: सः he, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, अपश्यत् saw, ततस्ततः here and there, प्राणिनः living beings, सुकृतं कर्म good deeds, भुञ्जानान् experiencing, च and, एव indeed, दुष्कृतम् evil deeds.
explanation: The mighty-armed Dashagriva saw living beings everywhere experiencing the fruits of both their good and evil deeds.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह । यमस्य पुरुषैरुग्रैर्घोररूपैर्भयानकैः ।। 7.21.11 ।।
transliteration: apaśyatsainikāṃścāsya yamasyānucaraiḥ saha | yamasya puruṣairugrairghorarūpairbhayānakaiḥ || 7.21.11 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, सैनिकान् soldiers, च and, अस्य his, यमस्य of Yama, अनुचरैः attendants, सह with, यमस्य of Yama, पुरुषैः by men, उग्रैः fierce, घोररूपैः of dreadful form, भयानकैः terrifying.
explanation: He also saw Yama's soldiers along with his fierce, dreadful, and terrifying attendants.

shloka_text: ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च क्लिश्यमानांश्च देहिनः । क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् ।। 7.21.12 ।।
transliteration: dadarśa vadhyamānāṃśca kliśyamānāṃśca dehinaḥ | krośataśca mahānādaṃ tīvraniṣṭanatatparān || 7.21.12 ||
translation: ददर्श he saw, वध्यमानान् being killed, च and, क्लिश्यमानान् being tormented, च and, देहिनः embodied beings, क्रोशतः crying out, च and, महानादं a great cry, तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् intent on intense wailing.
explanation: He saw embodied beings being killed and tormented, crying out with a great cry and intent on intense wailing.

shloka_text: कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः ।। 7.21.13 ।।
transliteration: kṛmibhirbhakṣyamāṇāṃśca sārameyaiśca dāruṇaiḥ || 7.21.13 ||
translation: कृमिभिः by worms, भक्ष्यमाणान् being devoured, च and, सारमेयैः by dogs, च and, दारुणैः fierce.
explanation: He saw them being devoured by worms and by fierce dogs.

shloka_text: क्षोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः । सन्तार्यमाणान्वैतरणीं बहुशः शोणितोदकाम् ।। 7.21.14 ।।
transliteration: kṣotrāyāsakarā vāco vadataśca bhayāvahāḥ | santāryamāṇānvaitaraṇīṃ bahuśaḥ śoṇitodakām || 7.21.14 ||
translation: क्षोत्रायासकराः causing distress to the ears, वाचः words, वदतः speaking, च and, भयावहाः terrifying, सन्तार्यमाणान् being made to cross, वैतरणीं the Vaitarani, बहुशः repeatedly, शोणितोदकाम् having blood as water.
explanation: He heard them uttering terrifying cries that caused distress to the ears, and saw them repeatedly being made to cross the Vaitarani river, whose waters were blood.

shloka_text: वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान्मुहूर्मुहुः । असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान् ।। 7.21.15 ।।
transliteration: vālukāsu ca taptāsu tapyamānānmuhūrmuhuḥ | asipatravane caiva bhidyamānānadhārmikān || 7.21.15 ||
translation: वालुकासु in sands, च and, तप्तासु hot, तप्यमानान् being tormented, मुहूर्मुहुः again and again, असिपत्रवने in the forest of sword-leaves, च and, एव indeed, भिद्यमानान् being cut/pierced, अधार्मिकान् the unrighteous ones
explanation: Ravana saw the unrighteous being tormented repeatedly in hot sands and cut in the forest of sword-leaves.

shloka_text: रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि । पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान्क्षुधितानपि ।। 7.21.16 ।।
transliteration: raurave kṣāranadyāṃ ca kṣuradhārāsu caiva hi | pānīyaṃ yācamānāṃśca tṛṣitānkṣudhitānapi || 7.21.16 ||
translation: रौरवे in Raurava (hell), क्षारनद्यां in the river of caustic liquid, च and, क्षुरधारासु on razor-sharp edges, च and, एव indeed, हि surely, पानीयं water, याचमानांश्च and begging, तृषितान् thirsty, क्षुधितानपि and hungry
explanation: He also saw them in Raurava hell, in the caustic river, and on razor-sharp edges, begging for water while thirsty and hungry.

shloka_text: शवभूतान्कृशान्दीनान्विवर्णान्मुक्तमूर्धजान् । मलपङ्कधरान्दीनान्रूक्षांश्च परिधावतः ।। 7.21.17 ।।
transliteration: śavabhūtānkṛśāndīnānvivarṇānmuktamūrdhajān | malapaṅkadharāndīnānrūkṣāṃśca paridhāvataḥ || 7.21.17 ||
translation: शवभूतान् like corpses, कृशान् emaciated, दीनान् miserable, विवर्णान् discolored, मुक्तमूर्धजान् with disheveled hair, मलपङ्कधरान् covered in dirt and mud, दीनान् miserable, रूक्षान् rough (in appearance), च and, परिधावतः running around
explanation: These miserable beings appeared like corpses, emaciated, discolored, with disheveled hair, covered in dirt and mud, and were running around frantically.

shloka_text: ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः । प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद्रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः ।। 7.21.18 ।।
transliteration: dadarśa rāvaṇo mārge śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ | kāṃścicca gṛhamukhyeṣu gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ | pramodamānānadrākṣīdrāvaṇaḥ sukṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ || 7.21.18 ||
translation: ददर्श saw, रावणो Ravana, मार्गे on the path, शतशो by hundreds, अथ then, सहस्रशः by thousands, कांश्चित् some, च and, गृहमुख्येषु in excellent houses, गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः with sounds of singing and musical instruments, प्रमोदमानान् rejoicing, अद्राक्षीत् saw, रावणः Ravana, सुकृतैः by their good deeds, स्वकैः own
explanation: Ravana saw hundreds and thousands of such beings on his path, but he also saw others rejoicing in splendid houses with sounds of music and singing, enjoying the fruits of their own good deeds.

shloka_text: गौरसं गोप्रदातारो ह्यन्नं चैवान्नदायिनः । गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः ।। 7.21.19 ।।
transliteration: gaurasaṃ gopradātāro hyannaṃ caivānnadāyinaḥ | gṛhāṃśca gṛhadātāraḥ svakarmaphalamaśnataḥ || 7.21.19 ||
translation: गौरसं milk products (or cows), गोप्रदातारो givers of cows, हि indeed, अन्नं food, च and, एव indeed, अन्नदायिनः givers of food, गृहान् houses, च and, गृहदातारः givers of houses, स्वकर्मफलम् the fruit of their own actions, अश्नतः enjoying
explanation: Those who gave cows enjoyed milk products, givers of food enjoyed food, and givers of houses enjoyed houses, thus partaking in the fruits of their own good deeds.

shloka_text: सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलङ्कृतान् ।। 7.21.20 ।।
transliteration: suvarṇamaṇimuktābhiḥ pramadābhiralaṅkṛtān || 7.21.20 ||
translation: सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः with gold, gems, and pearls, प्रमदाभिः by beautiful women, अलङ्कृतान् adorned.
explanation: This describes beings who were adorned by beautiful women with gold, gems, and pearls.

shloka_text: धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान्स्वतेजसा । ददर्श सुमहाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.21 ।।
transliteration: dhārmikānaparāṃstatra dīpyamānānsvatejasā | dadarśa sumahābāhū rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.21.21 ||
translation: धार्मिकान् righteous ones, अपरान् others, तत्र there, दीप्यमानान् shining, स्वतेजसा by their own splendor, ददर्श saw, सुमहाबाहू the very mighty-armed, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: The very mighty-armed Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, saw other righteous beings there, shining with their own splendor.

shloka_text: ततस्तान्भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः । रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाद्बली ।। 7.21.22 ।।
transliteration: tatastānbhidyamānāṃśca karmabhirduṣkṛtaiḥ svakaiḥ | rāvaṇo mocayāmāsa vikrameṇa balādbalī || 7.21.22 ||
translation: ततः then, तान् them, भिद्यमानांश्च and being tormented, कर्मभिः by deeds, दुष्कृतैः evil, स्वकैः their own, रावणो Ravana, मोचयामास released, विक्रमेण by valor, बलात् by force, बली the powerful one.
explanation: Then, the powerful Ravana, by his valor and force, released those who were being tormented by their own evil deeds.

shloka_text: प्राणिनो मोचितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा । सुखमापुर्मुहूर्तं ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम् ।। 7.21.23 ।।
transliteration: prāṇino mocitāstena daśagrīveṇa rakṣasā | sukhamāpurmuhūrtaṃ te hyatarkitamacintitam || 7.21.23 ||
translation: प्राणिनो the beings, मोचिताः released, तेन by him, दशग्रीवेण by Dashagriva, रक्षसा by the Rakshasa, सुखम् happiness, आपूः attained, मुहूर्तं for a moment, ते they, हि indeed, अतर्कितम् unexpected, अचिन्तितम् unthought of.
explanation: The beings released by that Rakshasa Dashagriva indeed attained unexpected and unthought-of happiness for a moment.

shloka_text: प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा । प्रेतगोपाः सुसङ्क्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन् ।। 7.21.24 ।।
transliteration: preteṣu mucyamāneṣu rākṣasena mahīyasā | pretagopāḥ susaṅkruddhā rākṣasendramabhidravan || 7.21.24 ||
translation: प्रेतेषु when the dead, मुच्यमानेषु were being released, राक्षसेन by the Rakshasa, महीयसा the mighty, प्रेतगोपाः the guardians of the dead, सुसङ्क्रुद्धाः very enraged, राक्षसेन्द्रम् towards the lord of Rakshasas, अभिद्रवन् rushed.
explanation: When the dead were being released by the mighty Rakshasa, the guardians of the dead became very enraged and rushed towards the lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः । धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां सम्प्रधावताम् ।। 7.21.25 ।।
transliteration: tato halahalāśabdaḥ sarvadigbhyaḥ samutthitaḥ | dharmarājasya yodhānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ sampradhāvatām || 7.21.25 ||
translation: ततः then, हलहलाशब्दः a tumultuous sound, सर्वदिग्भ्यः from all directions, समुत्थितः arose, धर्मराजस्य of Yama, योधानाम् of the warriors, शूराणाम् of the brave ones, सम्प्रधावताम् who were rushing forward.
explanation: Then, a great tumultuous roar arose from all directions, made by the brave warriors of Yama who were charging forward.

shloka_text: ते प्रासैः परिघैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः । पुष्पकं समवर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.26 ।।
transliteration: te prāsaiḥ parighaiḥ śūlairmusalaiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ | puṣpakaṃ samavarṣanta śūrāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ || 7.21.26 ||
translation: ते they, प्रासैः with spears, परिघैः with iron clubs, शूलैः with lances, मुसलैः with maces, शक्तितोमरैः with javelins and lances, पुष्पकम् upon the Pushpaka, समवर्षन्त showered, शूराः the brave ones, शतसहस्रशः by hundreds of thousands.
explanation: Hundreds of thousands of those brave warriors showered the Pushpaka chariot with spears, iron clubs, lances, maces, javelins, and other missiles.

shloka_text: तस्यासनानि प्रासादान्वेदिकास्तोरणानि च । पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव ।। 7.21.27 ।।
transliteration: tasyāsanāni prāsādānvedikāstoraṇāni ca | puṣpakasya babhañjuste śīghraṃ madhukarā iva || 7.21.27 ||
translation: ते they, पुष्पकस्य of the Pushpaka, आसनानि its seats, प्रासादान् its palaces, वेदिकाः its platforms, तोरणानि its archways, च and, बभञ्जुः broke, शीघ्रम् quickly, मधुकराः bees, इव like.
explanation: They quickly shattered the seats, palaces, platforms, and archways of the Pushpaka chariot, just like bees.

shloka_text: देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे । भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा ।। 7.21.28 ।।
transliteration: devaniṣṭhānabhūtaṃ tadvimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ mṛdhe | bhajyamānaṃ tathaivāsīdakṣayaṃ brahmatejasā || 7.21.28 ||
translation: तत् that, देवनिष्ठानभूतम् which was a dwelling place of gods, विमानम् aerial chariot, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, मृधे in battle, भज्यमानम् being broken, तथैव even so, ब्रह्मतेजसा by the power of Brahma, अक्षयम् indestructible, आसीत् remained.
explanation: Even though that divine Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was a dwelling place for gods, was being shattered in battle, it remained indestructible due to the power of Brahma.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्या सुमहत्यासीत्तस्य सेना महात्मनः । शूराणामग्रयातऽणां सहस्राणि शतानि च ।। 7.21.29 ।।
transliteration: asaṅkhyā sumahatyāsīttasya senā mahātmanaḥ | śūrāṇāmagrayāta'ṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca || 7.21.29 ||
translation: तस्य his, महात्मनः of the great-souled one (Yama), सेना army, असङ्ख्या countless, सुमहती very great, आसीत् was, शूराणाम् of brave ones, अग्रयातानाम् who were leading, शतानि hundreds, च and, सहस्राणि thousands.
explanation: The army of that great-souled Yama was immeasurably vast, comprising hundreds and thousands of brave warriors leading the charge.

shloka_text: ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा । ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम् । अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः ।। 7.21.30 ।।
transliteration: tato vṛkṣaiśca śailaiśca prāsādānāṃ śataistathā | tataste sacivāstasya yathākāmaṃ yathābalam | ayudhyanta mahāvīrāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ || 7.21.30 ||
translation: ततः then, वृक्षैः च with trees and, शैलैः च with mountains and, प्रासादानाम् शतैः तथा with hundreds of palaces also, ततः then, ते those, सचिवाः तस्य his ministers, यथाकामम् as desired, यथाबलम् according to their strength, अयुध्यन्त fought, महावीराः great heroes, सः च and he, राजा king, दशाननः Dashanana.
explanation: Then, those great heroic ministers of Ravana, along with King Dashanana himself, fought using trees, mountains, and hundreds of palaces, as they wished and according to their strength.

shloka_text: ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः । अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत् ।। 7.21.31 ।।
transliteration: te tu śoṇitadigdhāṅgāḥ sarvaśastrasamāhatāḥ | amātyā rākṣasendrasya cakrurāyodhanaṃ mahat || 7.21.31 ||
translation: ते तु but they, शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः whose limbs were smeared with blood, सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः struck by all weapons, अमात्याः ministers, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of Rakshasas, चक्रुः waged, आयोधनम् battle, महत् great.
explanation: Though their limbs were smeared with blood and they were struck by all sorts of weapons, those ministers of the Rakshasa king waged a great battle.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणैर्भृशम् । यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः ।। 7.21.32 ।।
transliteration: anyonyaṃ te mahābhāgā jaghnuḥ praharaṇairbhṛśam | yamasya ca mahābāho rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇaḥ || 7.21.32 ||
translation: अन्योन्यम् each other, ते those, महाभागाः great ones, जघ्नुः struck, प्रहरणैः with weapons, भृशम् fiercely, यमस्य च and of Yama, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, रावणस्य च and of Ravana, मन्त्रिणः ministers.
explanation: O mighty-armed one, those great ministers of Yama and Ravana fiercely struck each other with their weapons.

shloka_text: अमात्यांस्तांस्तु सन्त्यज्य यमयोधा महाबलाः । तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्षैर्दशाननम् ।। 7.21.33 ।।
transliteration: amātyāṃstāṃstu santyajya yamayodhā mahābalāḥ | tameva cābhyadhāvanta śūlavarṣairdaśānanam || 7.21.33 ||
translation: अमात्यान् तान् तु but those ministers, सन्त्यज्य abandoning, यमयोधाः Yama's warriors, महाबलाः mighty, तम् एव च and him alone, अभ्यधावन्त rushed towards, शूलवर्षैः with showers of spears, दशाननम् Dashanana.
explanation: The mighty warriors of Yama, abandoning those ministers, rushed directly towards Dashanana (Ravana) with showers of spears.

shloka_text: ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः । फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.34 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śoṇitadigdhāṅgaḥ prahārairjarjarīkṛtaḥ | phullāśoka ivābhāti puṣpake rākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.21.34 ||
translation: ततः then, शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः whose limbs were smeared with blood, प्रहारैः by blows, जर्जरीकृतः wounded, फुल्ल अशोकः a blooming Ashoka tree, इव like, आभाति appeared, पुष्पके on the Pushpaka, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: Then, the lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, with his limbs smeared with blood and wounded by the blows, appeared on his Pushpaka chariot like a blooming Ashoka tree.

shloka_text: स तु शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् । मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली ।। 7.21.35 ।।
transliteration: sa tu śūlagadāpāsāñchaktitomarasāyakān | musalāni śilāvṛkṣānmumocāstrabalādbalī || 7.21.35 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् spears, maces, nooses, shaktis, javelins, and arrows, मुसलानि pestles, शिलावृक्षान् stones and trees, मुमोच hurled, अस्त्रबलात् by the power of his weapons, बली the powerful one.
explanation: The powerful one indeed hurled spears, maces, nooses, shaktis, javelins, arrows, pestles, stones, and trees, empowered by his missile knowledge.

shloka_text: तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम् । यमसैन्येषु तद्वर्षं पपात धरणीतले ।। 7.21.36 ।।
transliteration: tarūṇāṃ ca śilānāṃ ca śastrāṇāṃ cātidāruṇam | yamasainyeṣu tadvarṣaṃ papāta dharaṇītale || 7.21.36 ||
translation: तरूणां of trees, च and, शिलानां of stones, च and, शस्त्राणां of weapons, च and, अतिदारुणम् very terrible, तत् that, वर्षं shower, यमसैन्येषु upon Yama's armies, पपात fell, धरणीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: That extremely terrible shower of trees, stones, and weapons fell upon Yama's armies on the surface of the earth.

shloka_text: तांस्तु सर्वान्विनिर्भिद्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च । जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.37 ।।
transliteration: tāṃstu sarvānvinirbhidya tadastramapahatya ca | jaghnuste rākṣasaṃ ghoramekaṃ śatasahasraśaḥ || 7.21.37 ||
translation: तान् them, तु but, सर्वान् all, विनिर्भिद्य having pierced through, तत् that, अस्त्रम् weapon, अपहत्य having repelled, च and, जघ्नुः they struck, ते they, राक्षसं the demon, घोरम् terrible, एकं one, शतसहस्रशः by hundreds of thousands.
explanation: But having pierced through all those weapons and repelled that missile, Yama's soldiers, in hundreds of thousands, struck that single terrible demon.

shloka_text: परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मोघोत्करा इव । भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमपोथयन् ।। 7.21.38 ।।
transliteration: parivārya ca taṃ sarve śailaṃ moghotkarā iva | bhindipālaiśca śūlaiśca nirucchvāsamapothayan || 7.21.38 ||
translation: परिवार्य having surrounded, च and, तं him, सर्वे all, शैलं a mountain, मोघोत्करा dense clouds, इव like, भिन्दिपालैः with bhindipalas, च and, शूलैः with spears, च and, निरुच्छ्वासम् breathless, अपोथयन् they crushed.
explanation: And all of them, having surrounded him like dense clouds surrounding a mountain, crushed him with bhindipalas and spears until he was breathless.

shloka_text: विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिक्तः शोणितविस्रवैः । ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत ।। 7.21.39 ।।
transliteration: vimuktakavacaḥ kruddhaḥ siktaḥ śoṇitavisravaiḥ | tataḥ sa puṣpakaṃ tyaktvā pṛthivyāmavatiṣṭhata || 7.21.39 ||
translation: विमुक्तकवचः with his armor loosened, क्रुद्धः enraged, सिक्तः drenched, शोणितविस्रवैः with streams of blood, ततः then, सः he, पुष्पकं the Pushpaka, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, पृथिव्याम् on the earth, अवतिष्ठत stood.
explanation: With his armor loosened, enraged, and drenched in streams of blood, he then abandoned the Pushpaka chariot and stood on the earth.

shloka_text: ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्तत । लब्धसञ्ज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः ।। 7.21.40 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sa kārmukī vāṇī samare cābhivartata | labdhasañjño muhūrtena kruddhastasthau yathāntakaḥ || 7.21.40 ||
translation: ततः then, स he, कार्मुकी one with a bow, वाणी (the warrior) Indrajit, समरे in battle, च and, अभिवर्तत advanced, लब्धसञ्ज्ञः having regained consciousness, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, क्रुद्धः enraged, तस्थौ stood, यथान्तकः like Yama.
explanation: Then, the bow-wielding Indrajit, having regained consciousness in a moment, stood enraged in battle like the god of death.

shloka_text: ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं सन्धाय कार्मुके । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं विचकर्ष स ।। 7.21.41 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pāśupataṃ divyamastraṃ sandhāya kārmuke | tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tānuktvā taccāpaṃ vicakarṣa sa || 7.21.41 ||
translation: ततः then, पाशुपतम् the Pāśupata, दिव्यम् divine, अस्त्रम् weapon, सन्धाय having fixed, कार्मुके on the bow, तिष्ठ तिष्ठ Stop! Stop!, इति thus, तान् them, उक्त्वा having said, तत् that, चापम् bow, विचकर्ष drew, स he.
explanation: Then, he fixed the divine Pāśupata weapon on his bow, and having told them "Stop! Stop!", he drew that bow.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे । मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शङ्करो यथा ।। 7.21.42 ।।
transliteration: ākarṇātsa vikṛṣyātha cāpamindrārirāhave | mumoca taṃ śaraṃ kruddhastripure śaṅkaro yathā || 7.21.42 ||
translation: आकर्णात् up to his ear, स he, विकृष्य having drawn, अथ then, चापम् the bow, इन्द्रारिः the enemy of Indra (Indrajit), आहवे in battle, मुमोच released, तम् that, शरम् arrow, क्रुद्धः enraged, त्रिपुरे at Tripura, शङ्करः Shiva, यथा just as.
explanation: Then, Indrajit, the enemy of Indra, enraged in battle, drew his bow up to his ear and released that arrow, just as Shiva did at Tripura.

shloka_text: तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत्विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् । वनं दहिष्यतो घर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः ।। 7.21.43 ।।
transliteration: tasya rūpaṃ śarasyāsītvidhūmajvālamaṇḍalam | vanaṃ dahiṣyato gharme dāvāgneriva mūrcchataḥ || 7.21.43 ||
translation: तस्य its, रूपम् form, शरस्य of the arrow, आसीत् was, विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् a smokeless circle of flames, वनम् a forest, दहिष्यतः about to burn, घर्मे in summer, दावाग्नेः of a forest fire, इव like, मूर्च्छतः raging.
explanation: The form of that arrow was a smokeless circle of flames, like a raging forest fire intensifying in summer, about to consume a forest.

shloka_text: ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे । मुक्तो गुल्मान्द्रुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति ।। 7.21.44 ।।
transliteration: jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe | mukto gulmāndrumāṃścāpi bhasma kṛtvā pradhāvati || 7.21.44 ||
translation: ज्वालामाली having a garland of flames, स that, तु indeed, शरः arrow, क्रव्यादानुगतः followed by flesh-eaters, रणे in battle, मुक्तः released, गुल्मान् bushes, द्रुमान् trees, च and, अपि even, भस्म ashes, कृत्वा having made, प्रधावति rushes forward.
explanation: That arrow, wreathed in flames and followed by flesh-eating demons, once released in battle, rushed forward, turning bushes and even trees into ashes.

shloka_text: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु । रणे तस्मिन्निपतिता दावदग्धा नगा इव ।। 7.21.45 ।।
transliteration: te tasya tejasā dagdhāḥ sainyā vaivasvatasya tu | raṇe tasminnipatitā dāvadagdhā nagā iva || 7.21.45 ||
translation: ते they, तस्य his (enemy's), तेजसा by the power, दग्धाः burnt, सैन्याः armies, वैवस्वतस्य of Vaivasvata (Yama), तु indeed, रणे in the battle, तस्मिन् in that, निपतिताः fallen down, दावदग्धाः burnt by forest fire, नगाः trees, इव like.
explanation: Yama's armies, burnt by the enemy's power in that battle, fell down like trees consumed by a forest fire.

shloka_text: ततस्तु सिचवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः । ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम् ।। 7.21.46 ।।
transliteration: tatastu sicavaiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ | nanāda sumahānādaṃ kampayanniva medinīm || 7.21.46 ||
translation: ततः then, तु indeed, सिचवैः with attendants, सार्धम् together, राक्षसः the demon (Ravana), भीमविक्रमः of terrible prowess, ननाद roared, सुमहानादम् a very great roar, कम्पयन् shaking, इव as if, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: Then, the demon of terrible prowess, Ravana, along with his attendants, let out a very great roar, as if shaking the earth. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः ।। 21 ।। Thus ends the twenty-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
